title: The Ascension and the Replacement of Judas
summary: Jesus shows himself alive to the apostles over forty days, speaking of the kingdom of God, and tells them to wait in Jerusalem to be baptized with the Holy Ghost. When they ask whether he will restore the kingdom to Israel, he says it is not for them to know times, but they will receive power and be witnesses to the end of the earth. He is taken up in a cloud, and two men in white say he will return the same way. In the upper room Peter proposes replacing Judas, and the lot falls on Matthias.

title: Pentecost
summary: On Pentecost a sound like a rushing wind fills the house where the disciples are gathered, tongues like fire rest on each, and they speak in other languages, so that pilgrims from many nations each hear them in their own tongue. Some mock them as drunk; Peter says it fulfills Joel and preaches Jesus crucified and raised. Asked what to do, he says to repent and be baptized, and about three thousand are baptized and join the apostles' teaching, fellowship and prayers.

title: The Lame Man Healed and Arrest of Peter and John
summary: At the temple's Beautiful gate Peter and John meet a man lame from birth, and Peter says, 'Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.' The man leaps and praises God. Peter preaches to the crowd, and the priests and Sadducees arrest them. Before the council Peter says there is salvation in no other name. Released, the believers pray, the place shakes, and they speak boldly.

title: Ananias and Sapphira
summary: The believers are of one heart and soul, and those with lands or houses sell them and lay the money at the apostles' feet; Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, is named as one who does. Ananias and Sapphira sell a possession and keep back part of the price. Peter tells Ananias he has lied to the Holy Ghost, and he falls dead. About three hours later Sapphira repeats the lie, and she too falls dead. Great fear comes on the church.

title: Stephen
summary: When Hellenist widows are neglected in the daily distribution, the apostles have the believers choose seven men, including Stephen and Philip, to serve tables. Stephen does wonders and debates in synagogues; opponents bring false witnesses saying he spoke against the temple and the law. Before the council he recounts Israel's history and accuses them of resisting the Holy Ghost. Seeing the heavens opened, he is dragged out and stoned, praying 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit', while Saul consents.

title: Philip and the Ethiopian
summary: Persecution after Stephen's death scatters the believers, and Saul ravages the church. Philip preaches Christ in Samaria, many are healed, and the sorcerer Simon believes and is baptized but is later rebuked by Peter for trying to buy the gift of God. An angel sends Philip to the road to Gaza, where he meets an Ethiopian eunuch, a treasurer of Queen Candace, reading Isaiah in his chariot. Philip explains it as good news about Jesus and baptizes him; the Spirit then carries Philip away.

title: Saul's Conversion
summary: Saul, breathing threats, goes to Damascus with letters to arrest believers. A light from heaven flashes around him and he falls and hears, 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?' and 'I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.' Blind, he is led into Damascus and fasts three days. The Lord sends Ananias to lay hands on him; scales fall from Saul's eyes and he is baptized. He preaches Jesus, is let down over the wall in a basket to escape a plot, and Barnabas brings him to the apostles.

title: Peter, Cornelius and the Gentiles
summary: A centurion at Caesarea, Cornelius, is told by an angel to send for Peter at Joppa. Meanwhile Peter, praying on a rooftop, sees a sheet with animals of all kinds and a voice telling him to kill and eat; he refuses, and the voice says not to call common what God has cleansed, three times. At Cornelius's house the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles as Peter preaches, and they are baptized. In Jerusalem Peter explains, and the believers glorify God for granting repentance to the Gentiles.

title: Peter's Escape and Herod's Death
summary: Herod kills James, the brother of John, with the sword and, seeing that it pleases the Jews, arrests Peter and keeps him under four squads of soldiers. The church prays. The night before his trial an angel wakes Peter, his chains fall off, and he is led past the guards and through an iron gate; at the house of Mary, mother of John Mark, the servant Rhoda is so glad she forgets to open the door. Later Herod, accepting acclaim as a god, is struck down by an angel and eaten by worms.

title: Paul's First Journey
summary: The church at Antioch sets apart Barnabas and Saul at the Holy Ghost's direction. They sail to Cyprus, where Saul, now called Paul, blinds the sorcerer Elymas and the proconsul believes. At Antioch in Pisidia Paul preaches in the synagogue, Jews oppose him, and he turns to the Gentiles. At Lystra Paul heals a lame man, and the crowds call him and Barnabas gods until Jews from Antioch persuade them to stone Paul and drag him out of the city. He rises, and they return, appointing elders.

title: The Jerusalem Council
summary: Men from Judaea teach that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, and Paul and Barnabas are sent to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem. After much debate Peter recalls God giving the Holy Ghost to Gentiles and says both are saved by grace; Barnabas and Paul tell of signs among the Gentiles, and James proposes writing to them only to abstain from pollutions of idols, fornication, things strangled and blood. A letter is sent to Antioch with Judas and Silas, and the believers rejoice.

title: Paul in Philippi
summary: Paul takes Timotheus, and a vision of a man pleading for help directs them to Macedonia. At Philippi Lydia, a seller of purple, is baptized with her household. Paul drives a spirit of divination from a slave girl; her owners have Paul and Silas beaten and jailed. At midnight an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer, about to kill himself, asks 'What must I do to be saved?' and is baptized. Paul later asserts his Roman citizenship.

title: Thessalonica, Athens and Corinth
summary: Paul preaches in Thessalonica's synagogue, a mob forms, and the believers send him to Berea, where people search the scriptures daily. In Athens he speaks on Mars' hill about the unknown god, saying God made all nations and will judge the world by a man he raised from the dead; some mock, but Dionysius and Damaris believe. At Corinth he lodges with Aquila and Priscilla, teaches a year and six months, and is brought before Gallio, who dismisses the case. Aquila and Priscilla also teach Apollos.

title: Ephesus
summary: At Ephesus Paul baptizes about twelve disciples in the name of Jesus, teaches in the school of Tyrannus for two years, and God works special miracles through him. People burn their books of magic. A silversmith named Demetrius stirs up a riot because of lost business for Diana's shrines, and the town clerk quiets the crowd. At Troas Eutychus falls from a window during a long sermon and is taken up dead; Paul embraces him. At Miletus he says farewell to the Ephesian elders, weeping.

title: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
summary: Paul goes to Jerusalem despite warnings, including Agabus, who binds his own hands and feet with Paul's girdle. Jews from Asia seize him in the temple and accuse him of defiling it. A mob beats him until the chief captain Claudius Lysias intervenes; Paul speaks in Hebrew, but they cry out when he mentions the Gentiles. He declares himself a Roman, divides the council by raising the resurrection, and more than forty men vow to kill him; he is sent by night to Felix at Caesarea.

title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa
summary: At Caesarea the high priest Ananias and the orator Tertullus accuse Paul before Governor Felix, who delays a decision and keeps him two years hoping for a bribe. When Festus succeeds Felix and proposes a trial in Jerusalem, Paul appeals to Caesar. King Agrippa and Bernice visit, and Paul tells his conversion story; Festus says he is mad from much learning, and Agrippa says, 'Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.' Agrippa says Paul could have been freed had he not appealed to Caesar.

title: Shipwreck and Rome
summary: Paul is sent to Rome as a prisoner under the centurion Julius, who treats him kindly. A northeaster hits the ship off Crete, and after days of storm an angel tells Paul that all will survive. After fourteen days the ship runs aground off Melita; the soldiers plan to kill the prisoners, but Julius prevents them and all 276 reach land. Paul is bitten by a viper and unharmed. Reaching Rome, he lives two years in his own hired house, preaching the kingdom of God without hindrance.
